docs.title: Welcome to DreamCision AI·SCRIBE
docs.text:
DreamCision AI·SCRIBE is your clinical documentation assistant. It listens to what you say during patient encounters, helps you organize chart data, and generates polished clinical notes. Your encounter data is stored on the DreamCision server on-site at Yarmouth Regional Hospital—your device runs the app, but it is not where the primary copy of patient information lives.

Think of it as a very good medical scribe that never takes a day off.

docs.title: What You Can Do
docs.text: Task How Dictate a note Press Record, speak, and the app transcribes everything Upload documents Photos, PDFs, lab results — drag and drop or use the camera Generate clinical notes Pick a note type and let AI draft your note in seconds Edit and copy Edit the output, then copy rich text directly into Word or your EMR Ask medical questions Built-in Q&A with evidence-backed answers Stay current Weekly literature summaries delivered to your workspace

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text:
Open your browser and go to:

dreamcision.com or notes.ieissa.com

Works on any modern browser — Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari — on desktop or phone.

docs.title: Need Help Finding Something?
docs.text: Use the search bar at the top of this manual to find exactly what you need. You can also browse by section in the left sidebar.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
If this is your first time, follow the path below:

  1. Creating Your Account — Sign up and wait for approval
  2. Signing In — Log in with your credentials
  3. Privacy & Consent — What you need to know about patient privacy
  4. Your First Time — A tour of the workspace
  5. Daily Workflow — Start dictating your first note

docs.title: Custom Note Types
docs.text: DreamCision comes with 10 built-in note types. If you need a different format, you can create your own.

docs.title: When to Create a Custom Type
docs.text:
Create a custom note type if you regularly produce notes that don't fit the standard types — for example:

  • "Operative Report"
  • "Pre-op Assessment"
  • "Fitness to Work Certificate"
  • "Medical Letter of Medical Necessity"

docs.title: Adding a Custom Note Type
docs.text:
1. Open AI Prompts (⚙️ in the left sidebar)
  2. Switch to the Note Types tab
  3. Click "Show add custom note type"
  4. Enter a name for your new type
  5. Optionally enter an initial template (you can edit this later)
  6. Click Add type

docs.title: Using the Template Library
docs.text: You can also click "Browse template library..." to open a catalog of pre-made templates. Pick one to pre-fill the name and template, then edit as needed before adding.

docs.title: Renaming a Custom Type
docs.text:
1. Select the custom type from the dropdown
  2. In the Note Types tab, enter the new name in the rename field
  3. Click Rename

Built-in note types cannot be renamed.

docs.title: Deleting a Custom Type
docs.text:
1. Select the custom type from the dropdown
  2. In the Note Types tab, click "Delete selected custom type"

This only removes the type — it does not affect any notes already generated with it.

Next: Evidence-Based Consult Comments

docs.title: Evidence-Based Consult Comments
docs.text: After generating a note, you can request an evidence-backed consult comment — additional clinical commentary supported by current medical literature, guidelines, and safety checks.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Generate your note first — the comment is based on the note content.
  2. Click the "Evidence Based Comments" button below the note.
  3. The system runs multiple checks in parallel:
  4. Searches medical literature for relevant evidence
  5. Checks for medication safety issues and drug interactions
  6. Identifies red flags and clinical concerns
  7. Scores findings by severity and confidence
  8. The comment appears in a separate card below your note with references listed.

docs.title: What You Get
docs.text:
• Clinical commentary relevant to your specific case
  • Severity scoring — findings are ranked by clinical importance (High/Medium/Low)
  • Confidence levels — how strongly the evidence supports each finding
  • References to supporting literature and guidelines
  • Medication safety alerts — potential drug interactions or dosing concerns
  • Red flag detection — warning signs that may need urgent attention

docs.title: Using the Comment
docs.text:
• Copy the comment into your chart as supplementary information
  • Review the references to verify the evidence
  • Use the comment to support your clinical reasoning — it does not replace your judgment
  • Your original note is unchanged — the comment is a separate addition

docs.title: If It Doesn't Work
docs.text:
Click "Retry Evidence Comment" if the first attempt doesn't produce useful results.

Related: Generating Your Note | Medical Q&A

docs.title: Literature Updates
docs.text: DreamCision automatically fetches and summarizes new medical literature every week, so you stay current without having to search for it yourself.

docs.title: Opening the Literature Panel
docs.text: Click Literature (📖) in the left sidebar:

docs.title: What You See
docs.text:
The panel shows a list of recent updates:

  • Title of the guideline, study, or update
  • Summary of the key findings or changes
  • Date of the update
  • Source information

docs.title: Refreshing
docs.text: Click Refresh to pull the latest summaries if new content has been added since your last visit.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Behind the scenes, the system:

  1. Fetches new clinical guidelines and research on a weekly schedule
  2. Processes and summarizes the content
  3. Makes it available in the Literature panel

You do not need to configure anything — it just works.

Next: Mobile Guide

docs.title: Order & Referral Requests
docs.text: After generating a note, DreamCision can automatically identify any orders or referral requests mentioned in your dictation and present them as individual, copyable items.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Generate your note
  2. If orders or referrals were detected, an "Order & Referral Requests" button appears
  3. Click it to open the requests panel

docs.title: The Requests Panel
docs.text:
Each detected request appears as a separate card that you can:

  • Review — read the full request
  • Edit — modify the text if needed
  • Copy — copy individual requests to paste into ordering systems

If no requests were detected, you will see "No requests were detected."

docs.title: Retry
docs.text:
If you think requests were missed, click Retry to run the extraction again.

Next: Medical Q&A

docs.title: Patient Materials
docs.text: DreamCision can generate patient-facing educational materials based on the clinical encounter. These are written in plain language for patients to understand — not clinical jargon.

docs.title: What You Can Generate
docs.text:
The Patient Materials dialog offers six categories of patient-facing materials:

  • New Diagnosis Information — Reliable information about a newly diagnosed condition
  • New Medication Information — Full details about newly prescribed medications
  • Current Visit Summary — Summary of today's visit and plan
  • Diet Plan — Nutrition recommendations tailored to the patient's condition
  • Exercise Plan — Physical activity guidance appropriate for the patient's status
  • Comprehensive Health Report — Comprehensive overview of your overall health and care

docs.title: How to Generate Patient Materials
docs.text:
1. Generate your clinical note first — patient materials are based on the encounter data and note content.
  2. Click the "Patient Materials" button in the Generated Note panel.
  3. Select one or more categories from the dialog (each has a checkbox).
  4. The system generates the selected materials in plain language.
  5. Review the output, edit if needed, and copy or print it for the patient.

docs.title: What Makes Patient Materials Different
docs.text:
• Plain language: Written at a reading level most patients can understand
  • Actionable: Focuses on what the patient should do, not clinical reasoning
  • Safe: Includes appropriate disclaimers and encourages follow-up
  • Encounter-specific: Tailored to the patient's current condition, not generic advice

docs.title: Using Patient Materials
docs.text:
• Print for the patient: Hand them the material at the end of the visit
  • Copy to the chart: Include it as part of the documentation
  • Edit as needed: Customize the material to match your specific recommendations
  • Combine types: Generate multiple types (e.g., diet plan + medication guide) for comprehensive patient education

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Patient materials are educational supplements, not a substitute for direct patient counseling
  • Always review the generated material before giving it to the patient
  • The system may not account for all patient-specific factors (allergies, cultural preferences, etc.)
  • For complex cases, consider supplementing with printed materials from professional organizations

Related: Generating Your Note | Reviewing & Editing

docs.title: Customizing AI Prompts
docs.text: A prompt is the set of instructions the AI follows when generating your note. DreamCision comes with well-crafted default prompts for each note type, but you can customize them to match your personal style and preferences.

docs.title: Opening the Prompt Settings
docs.text: Click AI Prompts (⚙️) in the left sidebar:

docs.title: The Templates Tab
docs.text: The Templates tab lets you view and edit the prompt template for each note type:

docs.title: Viewing the Baseline
docs.text: Click "Show baseline template" to see the original default prompt. This is read-only and shows what the AI was given before any customization.

docs.title: Editing Your Template
docs.text:
The main text area shows your current template for the selected note type. You can:

  • Add instructions ("Always include a differential diagnosis")
  • Remove sections you don't need
  • Change the tone or style
  • Add specific formatting preferences

docs.title: Saving Changes
docs.text: Click "Save template" to save your changes. They apply the next time you generate a note of that type.

docs.title: Reverting
docs.text:
• "Revert to server baseline" — Restores the default template for the current note type
  • "Reset all built-in templates to baseline" — Restores defaults for all note types (does not affect custom types)

docs.title: The Note Types Tab
docs.text:
The Note Types tab manages your note type list:

Here you can:

  • See all available note types (built-in and custom)
  • Rename custom note types
  • Delete custom note types
  • Add new custom note types

docs.title: Tips for Customizing Prompts
docs.text:
• Start small — make one change at a time and test the result
  • Be specific — "Include medication doses in mg" is better than "be more detailed"
  • Keep it clinical — the AI works best with clear, direct instructions
  • Use the baseline as reference — the default templates are well-tested; build on them rather than starting from scratch

Next: Custom Note Types

docs.title: Medical Q&A
docs.text: The built-in Medical Q&A lets you ask clinical questions and get evidence-backed answers — all within DreamCision.

docs.title: Opening Q&A
docs.text:
Click the Q&A button (💬) in the top bar:

The Q&A panel opens on the right side of your workspace.

docs.title: Asking a Question
docs.text:
1. Type your clinical question in the text area
  2. Press Send (or press Enter)
  3. The answer streams in real time

docs.title: Example Questions
docs.text:
• "What are first-line treatments for uncomplicated hypertension?"
  • "What is the dose of enoxaparin for DVT prophylaxis?"
  • "Differential diagnosis for acute onset hemoptysis in a smoker?"

docs.title: Attaching Images (Vision Q&A)
docs.text:
You can attach images to your questions — for example, a lab result or an ECG:

  1. Click the attachment icon in the Q&A composer
  2. Select an image file
  3. Ask your question referencing the image

The AI can see and interpret the image in context.

docs.title: Follow-Up Questions
docs.text: You can ask follow-up questions in the same conversation. The AI remembers the context of your previous questions and answers.

docs.title: Starting a New Topic
docs.text: Click "New topic" to start a fresh conversation. This clears the context so previous questions don't influence the new one.

docs.title: Evidence Citations
docs.text: When available, answers include an Evidence line showing how many sources (RAG and/or web) were used to generate the response.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Be specific in your questions for better answers
  • Include relevant patient details (age, sex, key findings) when asking about a specific case
  • Always verify answers against your own knowledge and guidelines — Q&A is a decision support tool, not a replacement for clinical judgment

Next: Literature Updates

docs.title: ASR Diarization
docs.text: Diarization automatically identifies who is speaking during a recording, separating the clinician's voice from the patient's voice (or any other speakers present).

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When diarization is enabled:

  1. The system analyzes the audio to detect voice changes.
  2. Each speaker is assigned a label (e.g., "Speaker 1", "Speaker 2").
  3. The transcription shows speaker labels before each segment of speech.

Example output:

Speaker 1: Good morning, how are you feeling today?

Speaker 2: I've been having some chest pain for the past few days.

Speaker 1: Let me examine that. Can you point to where it hurts?

docs.title: Enabling Diarization
docs.text:
1. Open ASR Settings (gear icon in the recording toolbar).
  2. Toggle Diarization to "On".
  3. Settings are saved automatically and apply to your next recording.

docs.title: When to Use It
docs.text:
Use diarization when: - You want a clear record of patient statements vs. clinician observations - You're documenting a consultation with multiple speakers - You need to verify what the patient said verbatim

Skip diarization when: - You're dictating solo (no patient in the room) - You're summarizing from memory after the encounter - You need faster processing and don't need speaker separation

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Similar voices: If two speakers sound very similar, the system may misattribute speech.
  • Background noise: Noisy environments can confuse the speaker detection.
  • Overlapping speech: When people talk at the same time, attribution may be incorrect.
  • Processing time: Diarization adds extra processing time to the transcription.

docs.title: Tips for Better Results
docs.text:
• Position the microphone to capture the primary speaker clearly.
  • Ask patients to speak one at a time when possible.
  • Review the speaker labels after transcription — you can manually correct them in the transcript editor.
  • Use a headset or lapel mic for the best speaker separation.

Related: ASR Settings | Dictating a Note

docs.title: ASR Settings
docs.text: DreamCision uses Whisper for speech-to-text transcription. You can customize how audio is processed using two settings: Streaming and Diarization.

docs.title: Accessing ASR Settings
docs.text: Click the Settings icon (⚙️) in the tools sidebar, then select the ASR tab.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
What it does: When enabled, transcription results appear in real time as you speak, rather than waiting for the entire recording to finish.

  • Enabled: You see text appear as you talk. Useful for long encounters where you want to verify accuracy mid-way.
  • Disabled: Transcription runs after recording stops. Faster overall processing, but no live feedback.

Default: Enabled

docs.title: Diarization
docs.text:
What it does: Identifies different speakers in the recording and labels them (Speaker 1, Speaker 2, etc.).

  • Enabled: The system separates patient speech from clinician speech. Adds processing time.
  • Disabled: All speech is transcribed as a single stream. Faster, but no speaker separation.

Default: Enabled

Learn more: ASR Diarization

docs.title: Saving Your Settings
docs.text:
Settings are saved automatically and apply to your next recording. They persist across sessions.

Related: ASR Diarization | Dictating a Note | Troubleshooting ASR Issues

docs.title: Adding Chart Data
docs.text: The Chart Data & Patient Info panel (left column) is where you organize all the information that will go into your clinical note.

docs.title: Current Encounter
docs.text: This is the main input area. It has two parts:

docs.title: Transcription (Read-Only Display)
docs.text: The top portion shows your voice transcription. This is read-only by default — click the ✎ edit icon to make changes.

docs.title: Encounter Notes (Editable)
docs.text:
The bottom portion is where you can type additional notes for the current encounter. Use this for:

  • Quick observations you want to add
  • Patient statements you want to record verbatim
  • Any information not captured in the voice recording

docs.title: Prior Visits (Historical)
docs.text:
This collapsible section is for information from previous encounters. Click the header to expand or collapse it.

Use this area for:

  • Previous visit notes
  • Past medical history relevant to the current encounter
  • Prior treatment plans or follow-up notes

Why separate it? The AI knows to treat this as background context rather than current findings, which helps generate more accurate notes.

docs.title: Labs / Imaging / Consults
docs.text: Paste lab results, imaging reports, or consult notes in this section.

docs.title: Automatic Date Detection
docs.text: The app automatically tries to detect dates in pasted content and classify items as current or historical. If a date cannot be determined, the item appears in an "Items Needing Date Verification" section with a warning icon so you can review it.

docs.title: What to Paste Here
docs.text:
• Laboratory results (copy from your lab system)
  • Radiology/imaging reports
  • Specialist consultation notes
  • Any other objective data

docs.title: Drag and Drop
docs.text:
You can drag and drop files directly onto any field in the Chart Data panel:

  • Audio files → processed as voice transcription
  • Images → processed by OCR (text extraction)
  • PDFs → processed by OCR (text extraction)

docs.title: Character Limits
docs.text:
Each text field has a character limit (50,000 characters). A counter appears when you approach the limit. If you exceed it, a warning message appears.

Next: Uploading Documents

docs.title: Managing Encounters
docs.text:
An encounter is a single patient visit or clinical interaction. Each encounter has its own transcription, chart data, and generated notes — completely separate from other encounters.

Think of an encounter like a fresh page in your charting notebook.

docs.title: The Encounter Strip
docs.text:
The active encounter strip is in the top bar:

Element What It Does Encounter name Click to rename your encounter + button Create a new encounter 🗑️ button Delete the current encounter Prev / Next Switch between encounters Recording status Shows if recording is active (Stopped / Recording)

docs.title: Quick Method
docs.text: Click the + button in the encounter strip.

docs.title: Full Method
docs.text:
1. Click Encounters in the top bar or left sidebar
  2. The Encounters panel opens
  3. Click + New encounter

docs.title: Naming Your Encounters
docs.text:
By default, encounters are unnamed. You should give them meaningful names for easy identification:

  1. Click in the encounter name field
  2. Type a name (e.g., "J. Smith — Chest Pain Follow-up")
  3. Click away from the field — the name saves automatically

Tip: Use a consistent naming convention, like "LastName, FirstName — Reason for Visit"

docs.title: Switching Between Encounters
docs.text:
• Click Prev or Next in the encounter strip to move between encounters
  • Or open the Encounters panel and click on any encounter to switch to it

Each encounter maintains its own data. Switching does not lose any work.

docs.title: Closing an Encounter
docs.text:
To close the current encounter (clear the workspace without deleting):

  1. Click Encounters in the top bar
  2. Click Close encounter

This clears the current view but keeps the encounter saved.

docs.title: Deleting an Encounter
docs.text:
⚠️ This cannot be undone.

Click the 🗑️ (trash) button in the encounter strip to delete the current encounter. All data for that encounter — transcription, notes, generated output — is permanently removed.

docs.title: Why Encounters Matter
docs.text:
• Separation: Each patient visit is isolated — no mixing of data
  • Organization: Name your encounters for easy reference
  • Queue isolation: The processing queue is scoped to the active encounter only
  • Privacy: Closing or deleting an encounter removes patient data from the active workspace

Next: Advanced Features — Customizing AI Prompts

docs.title: Generating Your Note
docs.text: Once you have your chart data ready, it's time to generate your clinical note.

docs.title: Step 1: Select a Note Type
docs.text: Use the note type dropdown in the top bar (or the mirror dropdown in the Generated Note panel):

docs.title: Available Note Types
docs.text: Note Type Best For Consultation Note New patient consultations, specialist opinions Follow-up Note Return visits, monitoring ongoing conditions Referral Letter Referring patients to specialists Admission Note Hospital admissions Progress Note / SOAP Routine progress documentation Discharge Summary Summarizing hospital stays and discharge plans Transfer Note Transferring patients between facilities Procedure Note Documenting procedures performed Summarize Creating a summary of lengthy chart data Custom (Free Form) Any format not covered above

docs.title: Step 2: Add Instructions (Optional)
docs.text:
Click "Add encounter instructions" above the note area to add special directions for this generation:

  • "Focus on assessment and plan"
  • "Be brief"
  • "Include medication doses"
  • "Emphasize the differential diagnosis"

These instructions are sent only with this generation request — they are not saved to your account.

docs.title: Step 3: Press Generate
docs.text: Click the Generate button (✓ Generate) in the top bar or the note panel:

docs.title: Step 4: Wait for Generation
docs.text:
The note streams in real time. You will see a "Generating..." indicator:

  • Generation typically takes 10-60 seconds depending on the amount of data
  • You can see the note appear word by word
  • If you need to stop, click the Stop button

docs.title: Step 5: Note Appears
docs.text: Your generated note appears in the right column, formatted and ready to review:

docs.title: What the AI Uses
docs.text:
The AI generates your note based on:

  1. Your chart data — transcription, typed notes, uploaded documents
  2. Your note type — determines the structure and format
  3. Your profile — your name, specialty, and location are included
  4. Your template — if you have customized the prompt template for this note type
  5. Your encounter instructions — if you added any

docs.title: Generation Failed?
docs.text:
If generation fails or produces poor results:

  1. Check your connection status (should say "Connected")
  2. Make sure you have chart data entered (the AI needs something to work with)
  3. Try again — sometimes a second attempt produces better results
  4. Check the Encounter Queue for any failed processing items

Next: Reviewing & Editing Your Note

docs.title: Daily Workflow Overview
docs.text:
Here is the typical flow for a patient encounter, from start to finish:

1. Start a new encounter
2. Press Record and speak
3. Add any chart data (labs, imaging, prior visits)
4. Select note type
5. Press Generate
6. Review and edit the note
7. Copy to your EMR or Word

Each step is covered in detail on the pages below.

docs.title: Quick Start (5 Minutes)
docs.text:
If you just want to get going:

  1. Press the Record button (🎙️)
  2. Speak naturally about the patient encounter
  3. Press Record again to stop
  4. Your transcription appears in the Current Encounter section
  5. Select a Note Type from the dropdown
  6. Click Generate
  7. Review the note, make any edits
  8. Click Copy Note and paste into your EMR

That's it. The pages below explain each step in detail.

docs.title: The Pages Ahead
docs.text:
Page What You'll Learn Voice Recording How to dictate using the microphone Adding Chart Data Typing notes, adding labs and imaging Uploading Documents Camera, file upload, drag-and-drop Generating Your Note Note types and the generation process Reviewing & Editing Editing, formatting, and copying notes Managing Encounters Creating, switching, and organizing encounters

Next: Dictating a Note (Voice Recording)

docs.title: Reviewing & Editing Your Note
docs.text: After the AI generates your note, review it carefully. You are responsible for the final content — always verify before using.

docs.title: Reading the Note
docs.text: The generated note appears in formatted view by default. Headings, lists, and paragraphs are rendered cleanly:

docs.title: Editing the Note
docs.text: Click the Edit button to switch to edit mode:

docs.title: Formatting Toolbar
docs.text:
While editing, use the toolbar to add formatting:

Button What It Does B Bold selected text I Italicize selected text H2 Insert a heading • List Create a bullet list 1. Create a numbered list — Insert a horizontal divider

docs.title: Editing Tips
docs.text:
• Highlight text, then click a formatting button
  • Type freely — the editor accepts any text
  • The formatting uses simple markdown (standard text markers)
  • Click Edit again to return to preview mode and see how it looks

docs.title: Copying Your Note
docs.text: The Copy Note button is the most important button in the app:

docs.title: What Happens When You Click Copy
docs.text:
Destination What You Get Microsoft Word Rich formatted text (headings, bold, lists preserved) EMR text field Clean plain text (markdown markers removed) Notepad Plain text

The app automatically detects the destination and formats accordingly. Just click Copy Note, then paste (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V) into your destination.

docs.title: Saving / Downloading
docs.text: Click the Save button (💾) in the note panel header to download your note as a file.

docs.title: Rating the Output
docs.text:
After generating a note, you can provide feedback:

Button Meaning 👍 Good — the note met your needs 👎 Needs work — click to suggest what should be improved

Your feedback helps improve the system over time.

docs.title: Evidence-Based Consult Comments
docs.text:
After generating a note, you may see an "Evidence Based Comments" button. Click it to get additional commentary backed by medical literature:

This generates a separate comment with references — your original note remains unchanged.

docs.title: Order & Referral Requests
docs.text:
If the AI detected orders or referral requests in your note, an "Order & Referral Requests" button appears:

Click it to review, edit, and copy individual requests.

Next: Managing Encounters

docs.title: Uploading Documents
docs.text: You can get information into DreamCision in three ways: camera capture, file upload, and drag-and-drop.

docs.title: Camera Capture
docs.text: Use the camera to quickly photograph lab results, prescriptions, or handwritten notes.

docs.title: On Desktop
docs.text:
1. Click the Camera icon (📷) in the left sidebar
  2. The camera modal opens with a live preview
  3. Position your document in frame
  4. Click Capture Photo

docs.title: On Mobile
docs.text: On mobile, tap Tools in the bottom navigation, then tap Camera. The phone's camera opens directly.

docs.title: File Upload
docs.text:
Use file upload for audio recordings, images, or PDFs already on your device.

  1. Click the File Upload icon (📂) in the left sidebar
  2. Select one or more files from your device
  3. The files are automatically processed

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text: Type What Happens Audio (mp3, wav, m4a, etc.) Transcribed using speech recognition Images (jpg, png, gif, webp, heic) Text extracted using OCR PDFs Text extracted using OCR

docs.title: Drag and Drop
docs.text:
The fastest method: drag files from your computer and drop them anywhere in the Chart Data panel.

The drop zone shows a visual hint when you drag files over it.

docs.title: Processing Queue
docs.text:
When you upload files, they enter a processing queue. You can see the status of each item in the Encounter Queue card:

Action What It Does Retry All Re-process all items in the queue Retry (per row) Re-process a single item Download (per row) Download the processed result Delete (per row) Remove an item from the queue Clear encounter queue Remove all items

docs.title: What Happens After Upload
docs.text:
• Audio files → Transcription appears in the Current Encounter section
  • Images/PDFs → Extracted text appears in the Labs/Imaging/Consults section
  • Processing takes a few seconds to a minute depending on file size

Next: Generating Your Note

docs.title: Dictating a Note (Voice Recording)
docs.text: Voice recording is the fastest way to capture your clinical encounter. Just speak naturally — the app transcribes everything in real time.

docs.title: Step 1: Start Recording
docs.text:
Click the Record button. You can find it in two places:

  • Top bar: The microphone button labeled "Record"
  • Left sidebar: The 🎙️ icon at the top

You can also find a round record button in the Chart Data panel header.

docs.title: Step 2: Consent Audio Plays
docs.text:
On the first Record press for each encounter, the app automatically plays a brief audio message:

"Recording with patient permission."

This is your reminder to ensure the patient knows you are recording.

docs.title: Step 3: Speak Naturally
docs.text:
While recording, the button changes appearance to indicate it is active.

Speak naturally. You do not need to use special commands or formal language. Talk as you normally would during a patient encounter. The transcription will appear in the Current Encounter section of the Chart Data panel.

docs.title: Tips for Better Transcription
docs.text:
• Speak clearly at a normal pace
  • Minimize background noise when possible
  • Medical terminology is handled well — use your normal clinical language
  • If you make a verbal mistake, just correct yourself naturally ("no, I meant 150 milligrams")

docs.title: Step 4: Stop Recording
docs.text: Click the Record button again to stop. Your full transcription appears in the Current Encounter section:

docs.title: Streaming (Real-Time Transcription)
docs.text:
By default, DreamCision transcribes your speech in real time. You will see text appear in the Chart Data panel while you're still recording, giving you immediate feedback that the system is capturing your words.

You can disable streaming in ASR Settings if you prefer to wait until the recording is complete.

docs.title: Speaker Diarization
docs.text:
If diarization is enabled, the system will identify different speakers and label them (e.g., "Speaker 1", "Speaker 2"). This helps separate clinician observations from patient statements.

Learn more: ASR Diarization

docs.title: Editing the Transcription
docs.text:
After recording, you can edit the transcription text directly. Click the edit icon (✎) next to the transcription to make corrections.

You can also type additional notes below the transcription in the same text area.

docs.title: Re-Transcribing
docs.text: If you want to re-process the full encounter recording (for example, if the first transcription had too many errors), click the Re-transcribe button that appears below the transcription area. This replaces the existing transcription with a fresh one.

docs.title: Multiple Recordings
docs.text: You can record multiple times in the same encounter. Each new recording appends to the existing transcription. This is useful if you have breaks in the encounter or want to capture different sections separately.

docs.title: Recording on Mobile
docs.text: On mobile, tap the Record button from the top bar or the Tools sheet. The experience is the same — speak, stop, and the transcription appears.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Recording
docs.text:
Problem Solution Microphone permission denied Check your browser's site settings and allow microphone access No audio being captured Check that your microphone is connected and not muted Transcription is garbled Speak more slowly, reduce background noise, or re-transcribe Recording button is greyed out Check that your connection status says "Connected"

docs.title: Privacy, Consent & Your Responsibilities
docs.text: This section covers what you need to know about patient privacy when using DreamCision AI·SCRIBE. Please read this before your first patient encounter.

docs.title: Nova Scotia's Personal Health Information Act (PHIA)
docs.text: In Nova Scotia, the Personal Health Information Act (PHIA) governs how personal health information is collected, used, stored, and shared. As a healthcare provider, you are responsible for complying with PHIA when using any tool that handles patient information — including DreamCision.

docs.title: What PHIA Means for You
docs.text:
• Collection: You can collect personal health information only for the purpose of providing healthcare to the patient
  • Consent: Patients must consent (expressly or implied) to the collection of their health information
  • Safeguards: You must protect health information with appropriate security measures
  • Access: Patients have the right to access their own health information
  • Complaints: Patients can file complaints if they believe their information was handled inappropriately

For the full PHIA legislation, see: novascotia.ca/dhw/phia

docs.title: What Happens When You Press Record
docs.text:
When you press the Record button for the first time in an encounter, the app automatically plays a brief consent audio message:

"Recording with patient permission."

docs.title: What You Should Do
docs.text:
1. Before pressing Record, inform the patient that you are using a digital tool to document their encounter
  2. Confirm the patient is comfortable with this — a simple "Is it okay if I record our conversation for my notes?" is sufficient in most routine care situations
  3. If the patient declines, do not record. You can still type notes manually into the app
  4. Document your consent approach in your practice according to your professional college guidelines

docs.title: What You Should NOT Do
docs.text:
• Do not record without the patient knowing
  • Do not use recordings for purposes other than clinical documentation
  • Do not share recordings with anyone not involved in the patient's care

docs.title: Where Your Data Lives
docs.text:
Encounter data is stored on the DreamCision server hosted on-site at Yarmouth Regional Hospital (operator facility)—not on your personal computer, tablet, or phone as the system of record. You use the app from your device (usually a web browser); the lasting copies of recordings, text, uploads, and generated notes stay on that hospital-site server.

Data type Where it is stored Voice recordings DreamCision server (processed and retained there) Transcriptions DreamCision server database Uploaded documents DreamCision server Generated notes DreamCision server database AI-assisted processing DreamCision server stack (same deployment—not on your device)

In this deployment, patient data is not sent to external consumer cloud services, AI providers, or unrelated third parties. If you are unsure how a feature connects to the network, ask your privacy or IT contact.

docs.title: Do
docs.text:
• Get patient consent before recording
  • Review every AI-generated note before using it — AI is an assistant, not a replacement for your clinical judgment
  • Keep your login credentials private
  • Use the app on secure, password-protected devices
  • Log out when finished, especially on shared computers
  • Follow your professional college's documentation standards

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Share your username or password with anyone
  • Leave your session open on unattended computers
  • Use the app on public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks
  • Enter patient data you do not need for the clinical encounter
  • Trust AI output without reviewing it — you are responsible for the final note
  • Use the app to make clinical decisions — it is a documentation tool, not a diagnostic tool

docs.title: Data Retention
docs.text:
• Your encounter data is stored on the DreamCision server at Yarmouth Regional Hospital (not as the primary record on your own devices)
  • You can delete individual encounters at any time from the Encounters panel
  • Follow your institution's document retention policies for how long to keep clinical notes
  • When you delete an encounter, it is removed from the active workspace

docs.title: Questions About Privacy?
docs.text:
If you have specific questions about PHIA compliance for your practice, contact:

Nova Scotia Health Privacy and Records Management - Phone: 902-424-5419 or 1-855-640-4765 - Email: phia@novascotia.ca - Website: novascotia.ca/dhw/phia

docs.title: What Is DreamCision AI·SCRIBE?
docs.text: DreamCision AI·SCRIBE is a clinical documentation tool that helps you turn patient encounters into polished clinical notes. Instead of spending time typing after a patient visit, you speak naturally — the app listens, transcribes, organizes your chart data, and generates a structured note ready for your chart.

docs.title: How It Works (In Simple Terms)
docs.text:
You speak → App transcribes → You add chart data → AI generates your note → You review and copy

That's the whole workflow. The app runs in your browser or device, but your encounter data is stored on the DreamCision server hosted at Yarmouth Regional Hospital—not as the lasting copy on your personal machine. In this deployment, patient data is not sent to external consumer cloud services.

docs.title: The Three Main Areas
docs.text:
The workspace is divided into three sections:

1. Chart Data (left side) — This is where your raw input goes: voice transcriptions, typed notes, uploaded documents, lab results, imaging reports.

2. Generated Note (right side) — This is where the AI produces your clinical note. You review, edit, and copy from here.

3. Tools (left sidebar + top bar) — Record, Camera, File Upload, AI Prompts, Encounters, Q&A, and Settings.

docs.title: What Makes It Different
docs.text:
• Hospital-hosted server — Transcription, storage, and AI-assisted steps run on the DreamCision server at Yarmouth Regional Hospital; your device is the client, not the primary place data lives
  • Voice-first — Dictate naturally; no special commands needed
  • Smart organization — Automatically separates current encounter data from historical data
  • Evidence-backed — Can generate consult comments supported by medical literature
  • Works on your phone — Full functionality on mobile devices

Next: Privacy & Consent — Read this before your first patient encounter.

docs.title: Using DreamCision on Mobile
docs.text: DreamCision works on phones and tablets. The core features are the same — record, generate, copy — but the layout is optimized for smaller screens.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) — The technology that converts your spoken words into text. Also called "speech-to-text" or "transcription."

Chart Data — All the raw information you provide: voice transcriptions, typed notes, uploaded documents, lab results.

Encounter — A single patient visit or clinical interaction. Each encounter has its own data and generated notes.

Encounter Queue — A waiting area for files (audio, images, PDFs) that are being processed. Shows the status of each item.

Generate — The action of asking the AI to create a clinical note from your chart data.

OCR (Optical Character Recognition) — Technology that extracts text from images and PDFs. When you upload a photo of a lab result, OCR reads the text from the image.

Prompt — The set of instructions given to the AI for generating a note. You can customize prompts to change how notes are written.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — A technique where the AI searches a knowledge base (medical literature) to support its answers. Used in Medical Q&A and Evidence-Based Comments.

Template — A pre-written prompt that you can edit. Each note type has its own template.

Transcription — The text version of what you said during voice recording.

docs.title: Note Type Settings
docs.text: You can customize which note types appear in the workspace and which one is selected by default when you start a new encounter.

docs.title: Setting a Default Note Type
docs.text:
When you create a new encounter, the note type dropdown defaults to a specific type. You can change this:

  1. Open Settings (gear icon in the tools sidebar).
  2. Find the Default Note Type option.
  3. Select your preferred note type from the dropdown (e.g., "Follow-up Note", "Consultation Note", "SOAP").
  4. Settings are saved automatically.

The next time you create a new encounter, your chosen note type will be pre-selected.

docs.title: Hiding or Showing Note Types
docs.text:
If you don't use certain note types, you can hide them to keep the dropdown clean. Conversely, you can show note types that were previously hidden.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Find the Note Type Visibility section.
  3. You'll see a list of all available note types with toggles.
  4. Toggle off note types you don't use to hide them.
  5. Toggle on note types you want to see.

Hidden note types are not deleted — they can be re-enabled at any time.

docs.title: Why Customize?
docs.text:
• Reduce clutter: Hide note types you never use to keep the dropdown focused.
  • Speed up workflow: Set your most-used note type as default to save a click.
  • Team consistency: If multiple clinicians share a setup, standardize on the note types your team uses.

Related: Note Types — At a Glance | Custom Note Types

docs.title: Troubleshooting ASR Issues
docs.text: Problems with speech recognition or transcription? Here are common issues and solutions.

docs.title: Transcription Is Slow
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Large chunk size setting - Diarization enabled (adds processing time) - Server under heavy load - Network latency

Try: - Reduce chunk size in ASR Settings - Disable diarization temporarily - Wait a minute and try again - Check your connection status (should say "Connected")

docs.title: Transcription Is Inaccurate
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Background noise or poor audio quality - Speaking too quickly or overlapping speech - Medical terminology not recognized - Wrong language model

Try: - Speak clearly at a normal pace - Use a headset or position the microphone closer - Minimize background noise - Edit the transcription directly in the Chart Data panel - Re-transcribe the recording with different settings

docs.title: Streaming Not Working
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Streaming disabled in settings - Browser compatibility issue - Network interruption

Try: - Check that streaming is enabled in ASR Settings - Refresh the page and try again - Try a different browser (Chrome or Edge recommended) - Check your internet connection

docs.title: Diarization Not Separating Speakers
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Similar-sounding voices - Overlapping speech - Background noise - Diarization disabled

Try: - Ensure diarization is enabled in ASR Settings - Make sure speakers don't talk over each other - Edit speaker labels manually after transcription - Try re-recording with clearer speaker separation

docs.title: Recording Won't Start
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Browser doesn't have microphone permission - Microphone is in use by another app - Browser compatibility issue

Try: - Check that your browser has microphone permission (look for the camera/mic icon in the address bar) - Close other apps that might be using the microphone - Try a different browser - Restart the browser

docs.title: Audio File Upload Fails
docs.text:
Possible causes: - File too large - Unsupported file format - Network error during upload

Try: - Check that the file format is supported (WAV, MP3, M4A, WebM) - Try a smaller file - Check your internet connection - Try uploading again

docs.title: Nothing Shows Up After Transcription
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Very short recording (less than 2 seconds) - No speech detected (silence) - Server error

Try: - Make sure you actually spoke during the recording - Check the server connection status - Try re-recording - If the problem persists, contact your administrator

Related: ASR Settings | Dictating a Note

docs.title: I Can't Sign In
docs.text: Symptom Solution "Account pending approval" Your account has not been approved yet. Wait for the administrator to approve your registration. "Invalid credentials" Double-check your email and password. Passwords are case-sensitive. Page won't load Check that you are using the correct URL: dreamcision.com or notes.ieissa.com Forgot password Click "Forgot password?" on the sign-in screen for a self-service reset. See Password Recovery.

docs.title: Recording Is Not Working
docs.text: Symptom Solution Browser asks for microphone permission Click Allow when the browser prompts you Microphone permission already denied Click the lock icon in your browser's address bar → Site settings → Enable Microphone No audio captured Check that your microphone is connected and not muted in your system settings Record button is greyed out Check that your connection status says "Connected" (top bar, left side)

docs.title: Transcription Is Wrong or Garbled
docs.text: Symptom Solution Words are misspelled Click the ✎ edit icon and correct the transcription manually Whole sections are wrong Click the Re-transcribe button to re-process the recording Medical terms are wrong Speak more clearly and slowly for technical terms, or type corrections Background noise in transcription Try recording in a quieter environment

docs.title: Note Generation Is Slow
docs.text:
Generation time depends on:

  • Amount of data — more chart data takes longer to process
  • Note type — some types generate longer notes
  • Server load — if others are using the system simultaneously

Normal range: 10-60 seconds. If generation takes longer than 2 minutes, check your connection status and try again.

docs.title: Note Generation Failed
docs.text: Symptom Solution Error message appears Check the error details, then try again Nothing happens Check that you have chart data entered — the AI needs input to work with "Disconnected" status Your connection to the server was lost. Wait a moment and try again.

docs.title: I Can't Upload Files
docs.text: Symptom Solution File type not accepted Supported types: audio (mp3, wav, m4a), images (jpg, png, pdf), PDFs File too large Try compressing the file or splitting it into smaller pieces Upload fails Check your internet connection and try again

docs.title: The Encounter Queue Has Failed Items
docs.text:
1. Open the Encounter Queue card
  2. Click Retry on individual items, or Retry All for everything
  3. If items continue to fail, check the file format and size

docs.title: Connection Status Shows "Disconnected"
docs.text:
This means your browser has lost connection to the server.

  • Wait a moment — it may reconnect automatically
  • Refresh the page
  • Check that the server is running (contact your administrator if the problem persists)

docs.title: The App Looks Different on My Phone
docs.text:
This is normal. DreamCision has a mobile-optimized layout with:

  • Stacked panels instead of side-by-side
  • Bottom navigation bar
  • Tools sheet instead of sidebar

All features work the same — the layout is just rearranged for smaller screens.

docs.title: Clearing the Queue
docs.text:
If you have a lot of items stuck in the processing queue:

  1. Click Clear Queue in the top bar (clears all items)
  2. Or click Clear encounter queue in the Encounter Queue card (clears only the current encounter)

docs.title: Still Having Problems?
docs.text:
If none of the above helps, contact your system administrator with:

  • A description of what is happening
  • A screenshot of any error messages
  • Your browser name and version
  • Whether it happens on desktop, phone, or both
